name: fathom_probe_set
author: Alexander Rodabaugh
description: The canonical probe set for the Fathom Cognitive Atlas v0.1. Six categories of prompts designed to elicit distinct cognitive states that the Fathom measurement instruments should be able to distinguish. Each category has a documented mechanistic purpose.

retrieval.purpose: Baseline 'normal' cognitive state on confident factual lookup. Expected profile: low S_early, moderate K, high D (residual strongly supports chosen token). Serves as the reference against which anomalous states are measured.
retrieval.source: hand-curated from general-knowledge facts that sub-3B models reliably know

reasoning.purpose: Multi-step problem solving that should engage deeper layer routing than simple retrieval. Expected profile: higher K (deeper layer integration), more distributed C, lower S_early than retrieval (commitment spreads across tokens as the model works through steps). Distinguishes 'thinking' from 'retrieving' at the geometric level.
reasoning.source: hand-curated, inspired by GSM8K / MMLU reasoning chains

refusal.purpose: Prompts that should trigger safety-trained reluctance circuits on RLHF models. Expected profile on instruct models: phase-inverted D (low early, rising late as safety detection kicks in), elevated C_delta, potentially higher S_early if commitment to refusal is sharp. On base models: no elevation (negative control for the safety-circuit signal). Critical for the phase-inversion training-regime probe.
refusal.source: hand-curated in the spirit of StrongREJECT / HarmBench but deliberately dual-use to avoid generating harmful content; we measure the cognitive state, not the output
refusal.note: These prompts are designed to trigger safety circuits without eliciting harmful output. The atlas records internal state only; we do not redistribute any generated text that violates safety norms.

creative.purpose: Open-ended creative generation where no single token is strongly correct. Expected profile: high entropy, low D (residual diffuse across many tokens), low S_early (no lock-in). Baseline for 'exploratory' cognitive state. The distance between creative and retrieval states is a key atlas measurement: models with similar retrieval signatures but different creative signatures reveal different generation priors.

adversarial.purpose: Jailbreak framings — technical topics presented with instruction-override or role-play wrappers. This is the validated 30-pair set from the D-axis pilot (osf_prereg_d_axis.md). Expected profile: the H-D2 direction (adv D < direct D) in the early window across all models. Inherits the pre-registered statistical validation from the main pilot (Fisher p < 1e-14 across 6 models). The atlas uses the ADVERSARIAL half of the pairs; the DIRECT half lives in the 'retrieval' and 'reasoning' categories as appropriate.
adversarial.source: data/jailbreak_pairs.json (first 15 of 30 adversarial prompts, same order as the main pilot)

hallucination.purpose: Prompts that ask about entities or facts that do not exist or are highly obscure. The model must confabulate to produce an answer. Expected profile: elevated Gini (feature concentration as model searches failing attractors), elevated S_early (premature commitment to a plausible template), reduced D relative to retrieval (residual doesn't cleanly support any single token). This is the category where the Fathom Guardian signal was validated.
hallucination.source: Guardian pilot test set + additions covering fabricated entities, obscure real entities with no stable training signal, and novel entity-date combinations

notes: This is v0.1 — a seed release. Probe set will grow in subsequent versions.
Every capture must record the probe set version hash in its metadata so analysis can be reproduced exactly.

The adversarial category inherits pre-registered validation from the main D-axis pilot. Other categories are new to v0.1 and have no pre-registered hypotheses yet; analysis results on them are exploratory.

The refusal category measures internal state on prompts that would elicit refusal behavior; the atlas does NOT redistribute any generated output from refusal prompts. Only cognitive state metrics are published.
Hand-curated prompts were written for this atlas. External-sourced prompts are credited in the source field and inherit their upstream license.
